documents.unit: Office of the Provost, Division of Academic Affairs
documents.title: Statement on Academic Integrity and Use of Artificial Intelligence
documents.summary: A short provost statement from August 2024. It bars student AI use in graded work unless a faculty member specifically authorizes it, leaves the decision to each instructor, and asks faculty to put their expectations in the syllabus.
documents.stance_why: The document says "students are not to use AI assisted technology in the classroom unless they are specifically authorized to do so by their faculty", which is a ban with a permission exception, so restrict. It also leaves the decision to faculty, but the university itself sets the default ban, so delegates does not fit.

units.why: The statement frames AI as a lasting fact that will "continue to shape our futures in education, the world of work". This is rationale about AI's place in education and work (P44 as the nearest type, since no duty to teach AI use is stated), so it is informs and neutral.
units.anchor: These tools are here to stay and will continue to shape our futures
units.frag_start: These tools are here to stay

units.why: The sentence says "we must always uphold our Community Standards and academic policies" and states an obligation to work "with absolute integrity and honesty". It is an institution-wide principle framing the AI statement (P56), binding everyone (must).
units.anchor: obligation to complete our academic and scholarly work with absolute integrity and honesty
units.policy: Everyone at Loyola has an obligation to complete academic and scholarly work with absolute integrity and honesty and must uphold the Community Standards and academic policies.

units.why: "students are not to use AI assisted technology in the classroom unless they are specifically authorized" sets the rule that applies when no authorization exists, i.e. a fallback default (P06). P01 fits less well because the ban is conditional on faculty authorization, not absolute. It covers "an assignment, a test, a quiz, or any deliverable that will be graded".
units.anchor: not to use AI assisted technology in the classroom unless they are specifically authorized

units.why: "whether you allow the use of generative AI or not in your classes is of course up to you" hands the allow/forbid decision to each instructor, which is P04, addressed to instructors with permission (may).
units.anchor: whether you allow the use of generative AI or not in your classes
units.frag_end: is of course up to you,

units.why: "you should include a statement in your syllabus stating your expectations regarding student use of AI" asks faculty to state AI expectations in the syllabus (P09), phrased as should, and it is communicated at course start.
units.anchor: you should include a statement in your syllabus stating your expectations

units.why: "not allowing AI to do the learning for us" gives the learning reason for limiting AI: AI should not replace the learning itself. This is the skill-building rationale (P41) rather than a prohibition on submitted work (P19), since it is stated as a shared aim, so should-not.
units.anchor: not allowing AI to do the learning for us
units.policy: Everyone should share best practices and not allow AI to do the learning for us.

units.why: "Students, you came here for your own education. With this opportunity comes an important responsibility" tells students they are responsible for their own education and its integrity. It matches P29 (students own what they submit) loosely; P32 is not chosen because it speaks of AI replacing thinking and this sentence does not mention AI.
units.anchor: you came here for your own education
units.policy: Students have an important responsibility to honor, respect, and carry forward Loyola's tradition of excellence in their own education.

units.why: "Loyola will continue evaluating and responding to the opportunities and challenges these tools present and we will share more updates" commits to revisiting the policy over time (P54).
units.anchor: Loyola will continue evaluating and responding to the opportunities and challenges these tools present

notes: Single short university-wide statement; no school or computing documents found, course layer deferred.
